title: Identification of Paleoproterozoic Metasedimentary Rocks on Hainan Island and Its Geological Implications
content: Detailed petrography and LA-ICP-MS zircon U-Pb geochronological analyses of metasedimentary rocks in the Jiangbian area are carried out in this study in order to reveal the formation age of Precambrian crystalline basement in the western Hainan Island, South China Block. Field characteristics of the metasedimentary rocks show that they underwent intense deformation and are crystalloblastic texture. They are mainly composed of quartz and muscovite. Zircon U-Pb dating results show that a representative metasedimentary rock sample yields two age peaks of 1736 Ma and 2339 Ma, suggesting that there is Paleoproterozoic crystalline basement on Hainan Island. Integrated with regional geological data, it suggested the protolith of part of the Baoban Group that was previously divided into Mesoproterozoic stratigraphic sequence was likely to be formed in the Paleoproterozoic. All of the Hainan Island, Yangtze and Cathaysia blocks were part of old landmass of China and recorded the assembly of supercontinent Columbia/Nuna.
